name: Sarmatism
summary: Sarmatism was the Baroque ideology of the Polish-Lithuanian nobility, who claimed descent from the ancient Sarmatians and saw themselves as an equal, free and martial ruling estate. It prized Golden Liberty (an elected, contract-bound king, a powerful Sejm, the liberum veto and a right of resistance), Catholic piety and ancestral custom, and it distrusted absolutism and foreign influence. It looked down on trade and held peasants as a lower, bound order.
scope: The noble ideology of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth from the late 16th to early 18th century at its 17th-century peak, based on the Golden Liberty constitutional order (Henrician Articles) and the szlachta's self-image. Excludes later Romantic revivals and the modern ironic use of 'Sarmatian'; answers on modern issues are mostly low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.role: Noble memoirist whose memoirs are a major primary source of Sarmatian outlook

keyFigures.name: Jan Długosz
keyFigures.role: Chronicler who first used the Sarmatian term in the 15th century

sources.usedFor: Noble equality, allodial land, peasant status, levy, taxes, origin theories.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The ideology predates welfare states; noble self-reliance and distrust of central taxation make a state health guarantee unlikely, though charity to the poor was a Catholic virtue.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage regulation was unknown; nobles lived off peasant labour dues and held peasants as a lower group, so mandated pay rises run against their interests.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nobles despised trade and trading itself yet profited from grain exports; no doctrine on markets versus government, so adherents split or are indifferent.

public-ownership.rationale: Land was privately held by nobles as allodial property and the crown had weak control; nationalised industry is alien and would extend royal power.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nobles insisted that no new taxes be imposed without the Sejm's consent and held tax exemptions, so heavy taxation of the landed wealthy would be resisted.

unions-good.rationale: Guilds and labour organisation belonged to the despised townsmen; nobles held privileged status over lower groups and had no sympathy for workers' organising.

property-fundamental.rationale: Noble liberty centred on inviolable privileges and property against the crown, protected by the right to resist a king who violated them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations did not exist; the noble ethos prized freedom from external controls, and regulation would mean more central authority.

cut-welfare.rationale: No welfare state existed; Catholic charity and hospitality were valued but state dependency was never discussed, so the answer is a split inference.

worker-ownership.rationale: Only nobles owned land and they regarded peasants as a lower order; collective worker ownership would overturn the whole social basis of noble rule.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Nobles guarded freedom from royal interference jealously; state spying on citizens would be read as an absolutist tool, though the topic is anachronistic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The issue did not arise; heavy drinking was part of feast culture but moral Catholic piety cuts the other way, so it is a genuine split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Noble freedom of speech at the Sejm and sejmiks was prized, and restrictions by authority would be treated as an attack on liberty.

strong-leader.rationale: Sarmatism was suspicious of absolutism and strong monarchs; the elected king reigned but did not govern and nobles could resist a ruler by force.

state-harmful.rationale: Nobles wanted a weak central state and prized liberty, but they still ruled through the Sejm, courts and the republic, so they were not anti-state.

limit-guns.rationale: The noble ideal centred on carrying the sabre and martial skill, and nobles bore arms as a mark of status and liberty.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nobles refused taxes for a larger standing army and relied on the noble levy, fearing a strong army would serve royal absolutism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Strict Catholic piety and the segregation of the sexes among nobles point against it, though the issue was not addressed directly.

rehabilitation.rationale: Honour culture involved duels and personal retribution; rehabilitation as a penal principle is anachronistic and ill-suited to this ethos.

traditional-family.rationale: Women were largely confined to the home with the sexes segregated, and the household under a patriarch was central to noble Catholic values.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Strong Catholic piety and the patriarchal noble household make this unacceptable, though the matter was not discussed in period sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholicism was central to Sarmatian identity, devotion to Mary and penance were emphasised, so abortion would be rejected.

more-religion-public.rationale: Catholicism was central to Sarmatian identity and public life, and it set Poles apart from their Muslim neighbours, strengthened by the Counter-Reformation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Nobles regarded peasants as a lower species and defended their privileges; remedial redistribution would run against noble interest.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Sarmatian culture had rigid gender roles and segregation treated as natural and ordained, so a constructivist view would be alien.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Preserving ancestral custom, dress, hospitality and the noble way of life against foreign fashions was a defining concern.

gradual-change.rationale: Sarmatian nobles defended the existing system of Golden Liberty and resisted reform, even when the liberum veto paralysed it.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Xenophobia and suspicion of foreign influence are noted in the ideology, though the Commonwealth was multi-ethnic and absorbed Tatar and other nobles.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The ideology was suspicious of foreign influence and prized its own Commonwealth as the best system in the world; supranational authority is anachronistic but contrary.

free-trade.rationale: Nobles exported grain and were exempt from tolls, but looked down on trade, so adherents are split on a topic never theorised.

nation-first.rationale: Strong pride in the Commonwealth's superiority and suspicion of foreigners imply national interest first, though it is inferred for a pre-modern context.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The ideology had a defensive military ethos against Turks and Tatars, but no doctrine of intervening for rights abroad; anachronistic, inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Nobles could block foreigners passing through their lands and were xenophobic, so openness is contrary though the question is anachronistic.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmentalism was unknown; the agrarian noble economy had no growth ideology, and the inference is weak.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; centralised state action over nobles' estates would conflict with their liberties.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The ideology looked to tradition, piety and martial virtue rather than progress; Enlightenment critics called it backward.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Entirely anachronistic and the ideology offers no basis for a view.

revolution-justified.rationale: The right of rokosz allowed rising against a king who broke noble privileges, and nobles could be released from obedience to him.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority rested on the equal votes of all nobles in the Sejm and sejmiks rather than on expertise, though the public beyond nobles was excluded.

central-planning.rationale: A weak central state and noble property make state direction of the economy alien, though the topic was never discussed.

socialized-markets.rationale: Neither worker nor public ownership of firms fits an economy of noble estates worked by serfs.

land-value-tax.rationale: Nobles resisted new taxes without Sejm consent and held estates tax-privileged, so a heavy land tax would be refused.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Taxes were limited by noble consent and family estates were protected; heavy inheritance taxes would hit noble estates.

basic-income.rationale: No such idea existed; noble ethos favoured hospitality and self-reliance over state transfers, so inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nobles shielded their own export trade and were exempt from duties, but had no concept of industrial policy, so split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: A weak crown with limited fiscal power could not and was not meant to direct investment; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Nobles considered all szlachta equal landowners with allodial land, so wide noble landholding was prized, though the peasants were excluded.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Estate economy depended on serf labour and noble property; abolishing money would be alien.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages would extend central authority over nobles and is foreign to noble self-rule.

one-party-rule.rationale: Golden Liberty rested on equal voices of nobles, the Sejm and sejmiks and the freedom to form confederations; single-party rule contradicts it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Commonwealth had a king, but elected and bound by contract, so a hereditary monarch is not what Sarmatists favoured and adherents accept a king only if elective.

democracy-best.rationale: Sarmatists thought their noble republic the best system, but it was a democracy of nobles only, so agreement is partial and inferred.

direct-votes.rationale: Nobles voted directly in the sejmiks and elections of the king, but laws were made through delegates in the Sejm, so the answer is split.

workers-councils.rationale: Political power rested with the noble Sejm; workers had no place, so councils of workers are contrary.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nobles could form confederations and resist, but no right of regions to leave the Commonwealth was an accepted doctrine.

natural-rulers.rationale: Nobles regarded themselves as descended from the conquering Sarmatians and peasants as a lower species, justifying noble rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The right of rokosz and confederation allowed armed resistance to a king who violated noble liberties, and the honour culture accepted duels.

war-builds-character.rationale: Military ideals of horsemanship and martial skill were central to the Sarmatian self-image.

separate-church-state.rationale: Catholicism was central to the ideology, though the nobility kept a semi-independence from clergy and the Warsaw Confederation guaranteed religious peace.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law came from noble statute, privilege and the Sejm; Catholic piety shaped culture but not a doctrine of scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Regional courts and the noble levy were public noble institutions and not private companies, but the privatised model is only loosely contrary.

military-superiority.rationale: Confidence in invincibility and martial excellence is noted, but a standing-army doctrine of superiority is not, so inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Sarmatian nation was a noble estate uniting Poles, Lithuanians, Ruthenians and Tatar nobles, not a single ethnic group.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nobles justified rule by conquest of the native population, but considered the order natural, rejecting class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Only nobles were equal and peasants were held as lower serfs, so equality of outcomes across society is rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Nobles' own origin myth is conquest of native populations and the legal landowning monopoly, so indigenous authority is contrary though anachronistic.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anachronistic; the ideology had no colonial concept and nobles resisted obligations, so weakly negative.

civilizational-union.rationale: Poland as a Catholic bulwark and kin of Orient culture offers mixed signals, with no doctrine of union of civilisation nations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Honour, hospitality and piety were stated virtues, while greed and trade were scorned, so open self-interest is not praised.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Nobles prized rights and liberties, including the rokosz and veto, above all, so duties first is contrary.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No relevant doctrine is documented; Baroque Catholic Providence is the nearest idea.

limit-population.rationale: Catholic piety and noble family values point against population control, though not discussed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anachronistic, though Sarmatism's agrarian values hint at distaste for industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The ideology's backward-looking tradition makes it hostile to disruptive change; Enlightenment critics saw it as backwardness.

human-enhancement.rationale: Catholic piety and traditionalism suggest rejection, though the question is anachronistic.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by equal noble votes and personal participation contrasts with algorithmic rule; anachronistic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic, with only a weak liberty-based inference.

restore-past-order.rationale: Sarmatism idealised ancestral custom and the ancient Sarmatian origin as a model against modern foreign fashion.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Commonwealth was defended as the best system in the world even as the veto paralysed it, so principle outranked results.

direct-action.rationale: Noble resistance through rokosz and confederations were direct action, but the Sejm and sejmiks were the normal channel, so split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contrary to the noble agrarian and martial society; anachronistic.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Social order was built on a division between nobles, clergy, townsmen and peasants.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A hierarchical order with noble privilege and serfs is incompatible with distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Estates produced grain for export for noble profit; the question is anachronistic.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nobles lived off peasant labour dues and would reject the idea that this is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Directly contradicts a noble social order and rule by the szlachta.

collective-farming.rationale: Nobles held allodial estates and worked them with serf labour; collective farming is contrary.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not a doctrine of the era, and the war ethos was martial rather than economic.

taxation-theft.rationale: Nobles resisted taxes not approved by the Sejm and enjoyed exemptions, but accepted taxes with consent, so split.

harm-principle.rationale: Piety and honour norms favoured moral regulation of conduct; liberty was a noble privilege, not a general principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights belonged to the noble estate as a privileged order, and peasants and townsmen lacked them, so group privilege is the idea.

conscription.rationale: The nobles had a duty of mass levy but a standing royal army needed Sejm approval and they resisted it; split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nobles valued the voice of the Sejm and veto above exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The ideology despised trade and entrepreneurship, so running the state as a business is contrary.

positive-liberty.rationale: Liberty meant freedom from royal interference for nobles, not material means for all.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Nobles believed in descent from conquering Sarmatians and treated peasants as a lower species, but this predates modern racial science, so only inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation was through noble local sejmiks and estates rather than parties, which resembles it, though the term is modern.

total-state.rationale: Rejected absolutism and prized a limited king with minimal state power.

national-rebirth.rationale: Sarmatists thought the Commonwealth already the best system, so they saw no need for rebirth until later Romantic revivals.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Commonwealth saw itself as defender rather than conqueror, but did expand eastward through the union; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Szlachta land was allodial with no service owed to a liege lord, rejecting feudal personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Nobles held peasants as serfs with legal priority over their courts and the right to their labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The ideology relied on faith, Providence and ancestral myth, though its values were not formulated in epistemology terms.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic piety and Providence imply universal moral truth, though knowable by faith rather than reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The noble republic pursued liberty and balance of noble privileges, but also invoked the Commonwealth's common good; split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No relevant doctrine and the ideology associated Jews with trade, but gave no position on Zionism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Polish and Latin were used and Latin was widely known; no language revival doctrine.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not a noble concept; the estate was the noble's own to command.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Public borrowing and countercyclical stimulus did not exist in the Commonwealth, and the sources give no basis for a view, so it stays neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Nobles linked liberty to property and exemption from royal impositions, but the claim is modern; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Honour, hospitality and piety mattered, yet law and constitutional limits were the core.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anachronistic; the Commonwealth was multi-ethnic and national self-rule meant the noble nation's self-rule.

force-without-un.rationale: The question presupposes the UN Security Council; the sources show only a defensive, Sejm-controlled war power, so no position can be inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Faith, Providence and Catholic piety were central and Enlightenment reason was the later critic of Sarmatism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No welfare state and no doctrine.

work-for-welfare.rationale: No welfare state and nobles scorned manual labour.

class-collaboration.rationale: Orders were hierarchical with peasants subordinate, yet a paternalist ideal is possible; split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The ideology revered ancestors, custom and inherited institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: A front of states dominated by Western powers is a modern idea, and Sarmatism's own distrust of the West was cultural rather than a diplomatic bloc.

workers-nation.rationale: The nation was a noble estate and workers were excluded; a working-class nation is contrary.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Women were largely confined to the home and the sexes segregated as the norm in noble society.

ban-interest.rationale: Catholic teaching condemned usury but no Sarmatist law is documented, and nobles borrowed.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nobles distinguished by estate and not race, and the Commonwealth was multi-ethnic with religious freedom, though contempt for peasants was strong.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Nobles saw the state as a republic of equals, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Oil, gas and coal industries were absent from the noble agrarian economy, so the sources give no basis for a position.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The ideology integrated Tatar, Ruthenian and Lithuanian nobles through the myth yet disliked foreign manners; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anachronistic conspiracy; xenophobia exists but no such claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: Noble equality did not distinguish parties; representation was by region and by estate.

national-mission.rationale: The Commonwealth saw itself as a bulwark of Christendom but not as an exporter of its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Patriarchal seclusion of women was accepted as natural, not as a structure of injustice.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nobles were suspicious of magnates and foreign kings, yet their own elite ran the republic; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Catholic piety speaks against eugenics, while it was not discussed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Prosecution of states for past abuses by their forces is a modern notion; the sources offer nothing on it for the noble republic.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nobles wanted the crown limited to little more than law and defence of the realm, with taxes and war needing Sejm consent.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Nobles integrated Tatars and others via the Sarmatian myth, and the ideology had no race-mixing doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: All nobles were equal but peasants were regarded as a lower species, so general equal worth is not held.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Socialism is contrary to noble order; the question itself is outside the ideology.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Sarmatian conquest myth was a source of pride, so it would not be understood as colonial.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Estates had separate law and privilege, with different courts for nobles, peasants and towns, and the Commonwealth held varied faiths.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion away from Catholicism was outlawed in 1668 as the Counter-Reformation intensified intolerance.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of Catholic Polish custom.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Catholicism central to society and education was church-linked.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Contrary to a ideology that kept the state weak even though surrounded by absolutist neighbours.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kings were elected and bound by pacta conventa and could not tax without Sejm consent, but consent meant the nobles only.

trade-surplus.rationale: Nobles exported grain but disdained trade, no mercantilist doctrine.

population-transfer.rationale: The multi-confessional and multi-ethnic Commonwealth had no such doctrine, though intolerance grew, as with the Arians banished in 1658.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Honour culture of duels and the martial ethos accepted force, though largely defensive.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Martial ethos but no theory of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The right to form confederations was a core liberty, so outlawing political groupings is contrary.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Golden Liberty was defined against royal domination, with nobles not subject to a king who could act arbitrarily and the right to disobey him.

separated-powers.rationale: The Henrician Articles required Sejm consent for war and taxes and a council overseeing the king, which is a check on the executive.

vanguard-party.rationale: Contradicts equal noble participation and rule by the Sejm.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Charity was a Catholic virtue but laws served noble privileges.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public council housing is a modern welfare institution, absent from the Commonwealth, and the sources give no position on it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Anachronistic though nobles would oppose labour agitation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Commonwealth was diverse and absorbed varied peoples through noble unity, yet nobles distrusted foreigners; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices were filled through noble election and royal appointment, not by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Noble protections against the crown were the heart of liberty and a king suspending them would be tyranny.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Nobles as grain exporters would resist price fixing, though the idea is anachronistic.

party-controls-media.rationale: Contrary to noble free speech in the Sejm and the rejection of absolutist control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Armed forces required Sejm approval and the king could not summon the levy alone; party rule is alien.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Nobles guarded privileges and could bar foreigners, implying restrictive access, with inference.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Nobles served as unpaid deputies bound by their sejmik instructions, but average-worker pay is not the doctrine.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Deputies were bound by their sejmik instructions, not parties, and the liberum veto reflected individual independence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The ideology held the Commonwealth the best system in the world and was suspicious of foreigners and foreign-elected monarchs.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The king could not summon the levy, declare war or send forces abroad without the Sejm's approval.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic hierarchy was accepted, yet nobles kept a semi-independence from clergy; no doctrine given.

clerical-rule.rationale: Nobles held authority and had semi-independence from clergy, so clergy ruling is contrary.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The noble martial ethos and pride in the Commonwealth contradict working for its defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Piety favours moral concern, while noble liberty resists censorship; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Elected kings could not name successors, and the system held to limits on rulers, so unlimited tenure is contrary.

recall-officials.rationale: Nobles could rise against a king who violated the law and instruct deputies, which resembles recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The noble army was a defensive levy, but no firm doctrine on alliances exists.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Estate and tenancy property and its landed ownership by nobles was central, but this is anachronistic.

people-in-arms.rationale: The noble levy (pospolite ruszenie) embodied the idea of armed citizens in place of a professional army, though limited to nobles.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The ideal was the landed manor, with contempt for trade and the town.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Division of a nation by an outside power is not addressed by the sources; the later partitions came after the ideology's peak.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Latin was widely known but often superficially, and xenophobia was said to weaken education.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Sarmatism held its own system and way of life superior to the West and others.

death-penalty.rationale: Strict honour and martial culture accept capital punishment, but no direct evidence found.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Catholic piety and segregation of the sexes mean opposition, though anachronistic.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The evolution controversy postdates Sarmatism, so the sources give no basis for an answer beyond general Catholic piety.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Strict Catholic moral norms suggest support though not documented.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nobility passed by descent, and the Sarmatian origin myth was a claim of descent from ancestors.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Commonwealth tolerated several languages among nobles but made no doctrine of language rights.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Henrician Articles pledged religious peace to dissidents, though later intolerance restricted it.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The ideology demanded conformity to custom in dress, manners and piety.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt relief for poor countries is a modern issue with no counterpart in the sources.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Landed property was the basis of noble liberty and they would not accept its transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The noble Sejm made constitutional pacts, yet the doctrine of rewriting the constitution is anachronistic.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty was held above all and restriction of liberties is the core fear of absolutism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Charity was a Christian value but international aid is anachronistic.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic for a 17th-century noble ideology, and the sources give no hint of a position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The king was freely elected by all nobles in the election Sejm and not parliament-appointed, which parallels this.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banks did not exist; the sources contain no basis for a view on monetary institutions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Noble property was protected as an inviolable privilege against the crown, not conditional on common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union is outside the period and the sources, so adherents have no stated view on how to classify it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not part of the doctrine and central regulatory power would be opposed.

collective-defense.rationale: The Commonwealth saw itself as a bulwark of Christendom against Turks, which suggests defence of allies, but inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Modern international law on occupation is not addressed in the sources, so the answer is left neutral.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The ideology was strongly Catholic and the crown was weak, so state control of the church is contrary.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The king reigned but did not govern, a symbolic head bound by law.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The sources mention confederations and rebellion against kings, but no doctrine on suppressing regional secession, so the position is unknown.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional sejmiks and courts retained autonomy within the Commonwealth, a federal-like structure.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The king was elected and bound by contract, so a sacred ruler is the antithesis of Golden Liberty.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax did not exist and only the principle of Sejm consent applied.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nobility was held to be a matter of descent from the Sarmatians, so character comes from innate blood.

space-expansion.rationale: Space travel is wholly anachronistic, and the sources give no basis for judging it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Commonwealth had king, senate and chamber of deputies and was compared to Rome and Greek poleis, hence a mixed constitution was praised.

leader-cult.rationale: Rejecting absolutism and a strong ruler, with the king as a limited officer, contradicts a cult of the leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law after separation is a modern question, and the sources show no position beyond patriarchal norms.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Outside the ideology; contrary to its order.

land-redistribution.rationale: Only nobles could own land and held it as allodial property, so taking estates for peasants would be an attack on noble privilege.

refugee-return.rationale: Rights of return for expelled refugees are a modern question not covered by the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on shared nationality abroad are modern; the Commonwealth's nobility was multi-ethnic, so the sources do not settle it.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Conversion away from Catholicism was outlawed in 1668, but nobles also valued religious peace through the Warsaw Confederation, so split.

women-must-cover.rationale: Women were confined to the home but a covering law is not documented.

common-currency.rationale: Anachronistic and suspicious of foreign influence.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Sarmatian myth linked nobles with Sarmatia including Lithuanians and Ruthenians, but the union was a noble union of the Commonwealth, not language-kin unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is a modern constitutional idea that the sources do not address.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A persecuted minority choosing between local rights and emigration is a modern debate the sources do not touch.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The ideology gave history to Providence, ancient descent and noble virtue.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust law is modern, and the sources give no position on competition policy in the noble economy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts of banks or firms did not exist in the noble agrarian economy, so no position follows from the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The noble majority and its Sejm were sovereign, but liberum veto protected individuals, so split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women were confined to the home and excluded from public life.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Nobles produced grain for export and avoided trade; split.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic and external regulation would be resisted.

moral-incentives.rationale: Honour and duty were praised but the economy relied on serf labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Confederations were armed groups of nobles, but not revolutionary in the Marxist sense.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Noble equality, privilege and descent defined the ideology, and attempts to create titles hierarchy were rejected but privileges kept.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The Sarmatian myth centred ancestors and the Commonwealth as the best system in the world.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The ideology saw itself as bulwark but not as tutor, though nobles considered peasants lower.

patriotic-education.rationale: Pride in the Commonwealth was central, but formal schools doctrine is an inference.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are a modern American-style policy debate with no counterpart in the sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform proposals are modern, and the sources give no basis for a view.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Theories about capitalism's crises are outside the period, and the sources give no position.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The question concerns post-imperial states; the sources do not address cultivating influence in former domains.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory debates over poor countries delinking from trade are modern and outside the sources.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist claim about workers in rich countries has no counterpart in the sources, so no position is inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nobles could bar foreigners and townsmen from their lands, but this is inference about free association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Henrician Articles and pacta conventa were entrenched constraints on the king that each had to swear and not alter.

decide-locally.rationale: Local noble sejmiks and regional courts held real power in the Commonwealth, and the crown was kept weak, so decisions as local as possible fit Golden Liberty.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The king swore the Henrician Articles and pacta conventa and nobles were freed from obedience if he broke them, so the ruler is firmly bound by law.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Henrician Articles bar kings from naming successors and keep free election with the estates.

minority-veto.rationale: The liberum veto let one envoy nullify a Sejm session's legislation and was prized as Golden Liberty.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Kings swore that subjects were freed from obedience if they broke the articles, and the rokosz gave a legal right of rebellion.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The Commonwealth had no concept of colonial partition; inferred as indifferent from its focus on noble liberties.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Golden Liberty made the noble Sejm the lawmaking body, with the king bound by the Henrician Articles.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from a hunting and horse-riding warrior culture and Baroque Catholic hierarchy of creation; animal welfare was not a concern.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: the landed nobility farmed and hunted without scruple, with ordinary decency toward animals assumed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Catholic charity and patronage of dependents were expected of the nobility, though the ideology stressed noble privilege more than duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Active participation in Sejm and local dietines was the core of noble citizenship and liberty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred disagreement from a culture that valued active political and martial participation.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: nobles held their rule as a birthright of the free estate, not something won by cultural persuasion of the governed.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anachronistic; the nobility profited from the Baltic grain export trade and had no reason to see it as exploitative.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices were reserved for the szlachta of the Commonwealth and foreign influence was distrusted; inferred support for native holders.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist parties did not exist; no inference is possible, so scored as indifferent.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from noble self-sufficiency on allodial estates and distrust of foreign influence.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: the nobility fought wars to hold or regain eastern lands such as Smolensk, but this was not a doctrinal demand.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anachronistic; the ideology placed political leadership with the noble estate, itself claiming a conquering Sarmatian descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the ideology bears on the question.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; the ideology opposed absolutism but did not address modern totalitarianism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for a position on the American Civil War.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from reverence for ancestors, custom and tradition.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Anachronistic; patriarchal noble society had no concept of male disadvantage programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: patriarchal household authority makes equal services for male victims unlikely to be endorsed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the Sarmatian self-image of a unique, ancestral Commonwealth liberty unlike Western absolutism.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nobles were the martial estate, but they feared standing armies and hetmans as a threat to liberty, so adherents are split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Anachronistic; household labour was assumed part of the manor economy and not wage labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed directly; the noble household was patriarchal and Catholic, so respect for parents is inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices were open only to nobles and filled through election at local diets and royal grant, with no competitive examination.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nobles disdained trade and valued sovereignty against foreign interference; inferred mild support for blocking foreign buyers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The nobility were devout Catholics and marriage was a sacrament not dissolved by law, so easy divorce is opposed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Deputies to the Sejm were envoys of the local sejmiki, bound by their instructions and answerable to them, as part of Golden Liberty.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; landed self-reliant noble households suggest private provision, inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nobles held land as allodial property, owned outright and heritable, with peasants bound to it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The Henrician Articles bound the king not to levy new taxes or wage war without the consent of the Sejm.

single-official-language.rationale: The Commonwealth was multilingual and religiously tolerant and the state did not impose a language, so imposing one is inferred as opposed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreigners could become landowning nobles only through naturalisation (indygenat), so land was kept for the noble estate.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Anachronistic; the system rested on legally unequal estates and the nobles defended their privileges, so outcome-based equality is inferred as rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Sarmatian culture prized lavish display in dress and feasting but also moral frugality, and adherents are inferred to be split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Sarmatian nobles guarded the Sejm control over war and a defensive posture; sponsoring foreign rebels is inferred as disfavoured.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anachronistic; Golden Liberty stressed sovereignty and consent and noble resistance to outside force, so intervention against allies is inferred as opposed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Corporations did not exist in the Commonwealth; the ideology feared magnate and royal influence over the Sejm, which does not map onto modern lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Sarmatism distrusted foreign influence and the Henrician Articles bar foreign meddling; inferred support for limiting foreign money in politics.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No documented population policy; the szlachta cared about noble status, not birth rates or immigration.

residents-only-property.rationale: Noble landholding and office were reserved to the szlachta, and the estate guarded its allodial land from outsiders; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Nobles lived from peasant labour dues and held peasants as a lower bound order; a state guarantee of work cuts against this.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Commonwealth knew no democratic-peace thesis; the nobles prized a martial culture but the claim about democracies was never addressed.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Henrician Articles gave a right of disobedience to a king who broke the law, but nobles valued law and custom, so no general right to disregard law.

non-intervention.rationale: The Commonwealth fought and meddled with neighbours and nobles valued armed honour; no principle of non-intervention is documented.

industrial-unions.rationale: Guilds were a lesser-regarded burgher matter; the nobility disdained trade and labour organisation, so industrial unions are unlikely to be endorsed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: No such conspiracy theory was central; Sarmatism was suspicious of foreigners and absolutism but is not documented as alleging minority plots.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Catholic nobility treated marriage as a sacrament and a legal institution that secured inheritance and noble status.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Golden Liberty rested on noble control of the Sejm and on consent to taxation, but a general public right of access to information is anachronistic; inferred.

local-production.rationale: The manorial economy was local to estates, yet it also exported grain; no local-production principle is documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: Noble politics ran through local sejmiks, confederations and the Sejm, formal assemblies, though local gatherings were important; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Golden Liberty put noble sovereignty and the Sejm above outside authority, so own law would outrank foreign courts; inferred from the constitutional order.

religious-nation.rationale: Sarmatism tied noble identity to Catholic piety, though 1573 Warsaw Confederation granted toleration and later Sarmatism was more intolerant.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of noble equality and freedom from foreign influence; the Commonwealth rejected subordination to other powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: the nobility prized local sejmiks and their own regional privileges, and distrusted central taxation.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of inviolable noble property held as allodial land; the question of common ownership is anachronistic.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anachronistic: communism does not exist in the period; the ideology is indifferent, though a hostile view of levelling property is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Anachronistic; the noble estate held authority by direct participation and public services in this form were not a concept.

religion-illusion.rationale: Catholicism was central to Sarmatian identity and piety, so adherents would not see religion as an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anachronistic; the ideology despised trade and gives no basis for a view on capitalism as a stage.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Sarmatism held a traditional patriarchal household order and the notion of economic transformation is anachronistic.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: household and the family estate were the nobility's domain, with no concept of public domestic services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not documented: Latin and Polish mixed freely in noble speech (macaronic), so purging is not a stated aim.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Golden Liberty rested on contract between king and nobility, as in the Henrician Articles, binding until both agree; internal nations are a loose analogy.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: communal property cuts against the doctrine of individual noble allodial landholding.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the Commonwealth was multi-ethnic and tolerant and the state did not steer settlement for nationalising ends.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anachronistic; neither capitalism nor communism existed, so adherents take no side.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the nobility's claim to Sarmatian ancestry and the Commonwealth's eastern lands; not a stated doctrine.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred that a Catholic noble ideology of the 17th century would reject it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from Catholic piety and the era's law; not stated in the sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Golden Liberty meant a king bound by law and a powerful Sejm, with free nobles resisting absolutism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Catholic piety was central but the Warsaw Confederation protected toleration among the nobility, so adherents were split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Commonwealth had no overseas empire; no stance is documented.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a Catholic outlook with no doctrine of obligatory jihad.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Their right of resistance applied to rulers who broke constitutional laws, not to rulers lacking religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Nobles took direct part in sejmiks and the Sejm but peasants and townsfolk were excluded, so adherents are split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the hierarchical order of nobles above peasants.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Baroque Catholic moral norms.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Catholic moral teaching.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anachronistic; the noble estate's order has no left-right axis to dissolve.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a noble ethos that disdained trade and leased labour to a bound peasantry.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from Catholic identity and wars against the Ottomans; not a stated doctrine.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority came from the free election of the king by the noble political nation under the Henrician Articles, within a Catholic order.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the strongly Catholic public culture.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed by the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a landed-noble economy resting on bound peasant labour.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The nobles prized themselves as a martial estate and the levy of the nobility defended Golden Liberty.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the nobles' insistence on legal equality within their own estate and a hierarchical order.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from distrust of foreign influence and kings' foreign alliances; not a stated doctrine.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Golden Liberty rested on free election of the king and a contract binding him, explicitly displacing hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nobles held trade and finance in contempt and lived off land; a user-owned banking scheme is inferred to be alien and unwelcome.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: International lenders did not exist; their dislike of foreign influence is the only basis for an inference.

property-franchise.rationale: The franchise belonged to the noble estate by birth, not to property or tax paid, and landless nobles voted; mild disagreement is inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Sarmatian culture stressed patriarchal gender roles and mastery over land and peasants; inferred disagreement.

reification.rationale: A modern Marxist concept; a landed estate ideology rejecting commerce as the organizing principle would reject its premise.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: No printing-press debate in this ideology; the sources do not support a direction.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Henrician Articles bound the king to law and the Sejm and gave nobles a right to disobey a king who broke it, which is rule by known standing law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The vote was limited to one estate, the szlachta, which claimed a Sarmatian origin but included Ruthenian and Lithuanian nobles; split between ethnic and estate logic.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; no position can be inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: Sejm sessions were public among nobles but traceability of records was not a theme; no sourced position.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Sarmatism was strongly Catholic, but the Commonwealth kept religious peace under the Henrician Articles, so legal restriction is inferred as unlikely.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Nobles disdained trade and kept religious peace by law; an organised boycott is not documented and is inferred as unwelcome.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sarmatians valued assemblies of the whole noble estate but through elections and sejmiks, not lot, and excluded commoners; no clear stance.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Sarmatist piety was Counter-Reformation Catholicism tied to ancestral custom, so revising inherited doctrine ran against its core.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sarmatism prized equality among nobles and opposed magnate domination, though it defended noble privilege against peasants; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: A Baroque Catholic, martial noble culture would not accept open homosexual service; anachronistic, so inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Sarmatism was strongly Catholic and tied national identity to piety, so state promotion of atheism is far outside it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nobles guarded their own courts and arms and saw order as upheld by the estates; abolishing police and prisons is anachronistic, inferred.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Golden Liberty required near-consensus among nobles and let minorities block decisions, which favours power-sharing over simple majority rule; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Charity to the poor was a Catholic virtue and nobles disliked central taxation, so private help is favoured; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Kings were elected for life and deputies sat per session; term limits were not a Sarmatian theme.

vote-delegation.rationale: Local sejmiks gave deputies binding instructions they had to follow, which resembles delegation, though not issue-by-issue or revocable; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern issue unknown to the movement; inferred neutral.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Catholic, patriarchal noble culture excluded women from church office; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The sources describe patriarchal gender roles in noble households, so marital authority held by the husband was normal.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The franchise and Golden Liberty belonged to the noble estate; foreigners voting in any elections is inferred as unthinkable.

rent-control.rationale: The szlachta were landowners living off estates and rents, so a legal cap on rents is inferred as against their interest.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyrights are anachronistic; the nobility's regime of privileges and property rights suggests opposition to abolishing them.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from a noble ideal of the free, armed citizen-warrior, not state-drilled youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic and the ideology gives no basis for an answer.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The ideology distrusted foreign influence and kings imposed from abroad, so foreign garrisons are inferred as against Golden Liberty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal genocide recognition is anachronistic and the sources do not address it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The nobles looked down on trade and lived from landed property and peasant labour, so income reflecting ownership was normal.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Sarmatian ideal was martial and the noble was expected to defend himself, family and Commonwealth by arms.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The central myth of Sarmatism is that the nobility descended unbroken from the ancient Sarmatians.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from a patriarchal, estate-based society; gender theory is anachronistic.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from a patriarchal noble order in which women's roles were fixed; the question is anachronistic.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the martial Catholic ethos honouring those who fell fighting for faith and Commonwealth; the sources do not discuss martyrdom.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Sarmatism was bound up with Counter-Reformation Catholic piety and the Commonwealth as defender of Christendom, inferred as a good-versus-evil framing.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora homelands are anachronistic and the ideology gives no basis for an answer.

culture-before-state.rationale: The noble nation was already identified with its constitutional state, Golden Liberty, so cultural renewal first is not its framing.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from a traditional Catholic piety; not discussed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from a traditional Catholic piety that treated scripture and tradition as authoritative; not discussed in the sources.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Nobles left trade largely to others, but the political nation was the noble estate itself, so no policy of majority economic control is attested; inferred mild disagreement.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The ideology concerned the noble estate within a multi-ethnic Commonwealth, and has no clear stance on merging regions by people.

missingStatements.text: Rulers should be chosen by election among the political nation rather than inherit the throne.
missingStatements.rationale: The Henrician Articles bar kings from naming successors and keep free election with the estates.

missingStatements.text: A single member of a legislature should be able to block a law by veto.
missingStatements.rationale: The liberum veto let one envoy nullify a Sejm session's legislation and was prized as Golden Liberty.

missingStatements.text: Subjects have a right to resist a ruler who breaks the constitutional laws and privileges.
missingStatements.rationale: Kings swore that subjects were freed from obedience if they broke the articles, and the rokosz gave a legal right of rebellion.

notes: The Sarmatian nobility's liberty was a privilege of the noble estate only (about 10-15% of the population), so many answers on equality and democracy differ depending on whether 'people' means nobles or everyone. Later Counter-Reformation Sarmatism was more intolerant than the 1573 Warsaw Confederation settlement.
